title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Page heading: 'Foncteurs de De Rham généralisés'. The page is a list of definitions, an axiomatic set-up for de Rham-type cochain algebras on simplicial sets over a base ring k. It belongs to the 1976 IHÉS talk on the divided-power de Rham complex.

1. Grothendieck considers contravariant functors C** : (Sf)^op → BD. Here Sf is (very probably) the category of simplicial sets. BD is the category of bigraded, alternating (graded-commutative, x^2 = 0 in odd degree), differential k-algebras. The conditions are bidegrees ≥ 0, differential of degree +1 in one of the gradings, '……' (further conditions left unspecified), and possibly augmented.

2. He restricts to functors sending arbitrary colimits ('lim' underlined, i.e. lim→) of simplicial sets to limits. Such functors are 'representable': determined by their values on the standard simplices Δ^n. So they are the same thing as simplicial objects in BD, i.e. functors Δ^op → BD, n ↦ C**_n. The transcription's word 'cosimpliciales' conflicts with the displayed Δ° → D; the formula indicates simplicial objects. One recovers C**(X) = Hom_{sSet}(X, C**_•), an end over Δ.

3. He identifies the two kinds of objects: C** = C**_• = (C**_n)_{n≥0}. Morphisms of functors correspond to morphisms of simplicial objects respecting all structures.

4. To C** is attached its 'de Rham cohomology' functor H**_C(X) = H**(C**(X)), valued in bigraded alternating algebras.

5. The page breaks off defining 'admissible' C**: those for which, for every X, some property holds. The expected continuation is a Poincaré lemma (acyclicity of each C_n) plus an extension or Kan condition, so that H_C(X) computes H*(X,k), perhaps with an extra weight grading.

This is exactly the framework of Sullivan's polynomial forms ∇(n,*), and of H. Cartan's 'théories cohomologiques' and Bousfield–Gugenheim (all c. 1976). The second grading is presumably a polynomial/weight degree. In the intended application the simplicial algebra is the divided-power polynomial de Rham complex of the simplices over Z or F_p, aimed at a commutative-type de Rham model in arbitrary characteristic.
errors: No mathematical error on the page itself; the definition of 'admissible' is unfinished.

Possible slip, or transcription error: the text calls the objects 'cosimpliciales' while writing Δ° → D. Colimit-to-limit contravariant functors on sSet correspond to simplicial objects Δ^op → BD (like Sullivan's ∇(•,*)).

Implicit caveat not addressed on the page: over F_p no functorial strictly commutative cochain algebra can be quasi-isomorphic, as an algebra, to singular cochains, because Steenrod operations obstruct this. The 'admissibility' condition must therefore be weaker than an algebra quasi-isomorphism with cochains, or must use the bigrading or divided powers to circumvent this.

ideas.what: Contravariant functors from simplicial sets to (bigraded) CDGAs that turn colimits into limits are equivalent to simplicial CDGAs, via C(X) = Hom(X, C_•).
ideas.modern_name: Representable / Kan-extended functors; simplicial CDGA of polynomial forms (A_PL = Hom(X, ∇(•,*)))

ideas.what: De Rham cohomology functor attached to a simplicial differential algebra, H_C(X) = H(C(X)), with an 'admissibility' axiom ensuring it computes ordinary cohomology.
ideas.modern_name: Axiomatic de Rham theorem for simplicial DGAs (Poincaré lemma + extendability)

ideas.what: Bigraded version (extra weight/polynomial grading), intended for divided-power polynomial forms over arbitrary k.
ideas.modern_name: Integral/divided-power simplicial de Rham forms (cf. Cenkl–Porter, Karoubi's de Rham complexes over Z)

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up a general category of 'generalized de Rham functors' (bigraded alternating simplicial differential algebras) and starts to define an 'admissibility' notion. This is apparently aimed at classifying or comparing all such de Rham models, including the divided-power one, over an arbitrary base ring k. This axiomatics in the bigraded, arbitrary-characteristic setting was developed in parallel with Cartan and Bousfield–Gugenheim but never published by him.
missed.quote: On s'intéresse aux C** (dits admissibles) pour lesquels pour tout X,
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Only mildly. Integral and characteristic-p commutative-type cochain models (divided-power forms, Cenkl–Porter, Karoubi, E∞ and derived-commutative approaches) are an active topic. Grothendieck's bigraded axiomatics might illuminate what structure survives in characteristic p, but this page alone gives only definitions.

deep.surprise_reason: Definitional set-up essentially matching Sullivan, Cartan and Bousfield–Gugenheim (1976). The bigraded, arbitrary-k framing aimed at divided-power forms is a modestly interesting unpublished detail, but no results appear on this page.
transcription_corrections: Heading is 'Foncteurs de De Rham généralisés' (correct).
'h[?] anguraires' is uncertain: likely 'augmentées' or similar. '(i.e. à p.d. bidegrés positifs' is probably '(i.e. à degrés {bidegrés} positifs'.
First 'lim' (underlined) should be read as lim→ (colimits) of Sf, sent to lim← (limits).

'Ils [-donnent-] des s'interprètent' is more plausibly 'Ils peuvent donc s'interpréter (particulièrement) comme des k-algèbres bigraduées alternées … simpliciales'. The word read as 'cosimpliciales' is likely '½ simpliciales' or 'simpliciales', consistent with Δ° → D.
Target in the displayed functor is the category BD (written '= 𝔅𝔇' above), so Δ° → 𝔅𝔇.
Formula: ℋ**_C(X) = H**(C**(X)); the subscript on H is not 𝒞.
